rules.sentence: When evaluating patients with suspected osteomyelitis, the initial imaging step is typically plain radiography.
Plain radiography identifies bony abnormalities and may help exclude other diagnoses, such as stress fractures or bone tumors.
Soft tissue changes, such as blurring of soft tissue planes and muscle swelling, can be early radiographic indicators of osteomyelitis.
However, radiographic changes may not be visible until 10 to 14 days after the onset of infection.
Further imaging is warranted if clinical suspicion of osteomyelitis remains high despite normal-appearing radiographs.
